2) Expected average tokens per request (or average response length in tokens) and daily active users (ballpark).
3) Commitment horizon for reserved capacity if you evaluate Dedicated (12 / 24 months).

Attached is a one-page readiness checklist and an initial usage estimate CSV I threw together from the numbers you shared. Hi Samantha / Procurement —

Thanks for the details — I put together a concise cost model (attached) and a summary below. These are ballpark numbers to help you compare economics and operational tradeoffs. Happy to walk through line-by-line.

Assumptions (from thread): 1,200 tokens/req, estimated monthly requests — 60k DAU * 20 avg requests/day = 1.2M requests/month ≈ 1.44B tokens/month.

Options (ballpark):

1) Hosted API (no commit)
- Unit price (generation+context): $0.60 per 1k tokens ($0.0006 / token)
- Estimated monthly bill: 1.44B tokens * $0.0006 = $864,000 / month
- Pros: fastest time-to-value, no infra commitments, built-in fallbacks and managed compliance (SOC2).
- Cons: unit economics worse at scale; per-token is linear to usage.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — 12-month commit example
- 1x Dedicated pool (GPU-equivalent capacity sized for ~300 QPS sustained, with short bursts): $28,000 / month (12-mo commit)
- Included throughput: baseline supports ~300 QPS steady; burst buffer handles short spikes to ~400 QPS for up to X minutes per hour (we tune policies per customer)
- Overage / burst consumed beyond policy: $0.35 per 1k tokens
- Estimated monthly token handling cost (if fully using pool capacity): effectively ~ $28k/month + small variable costs — substantially cheaper than hosted for steady high-volume workloads

3) Dedicated — 24-month commit (better unit economics)
- 24-mo pricing example: $24,000 / month
- Same included throughput; lower committed rate and slightly lower overage ($0.30 per 1k tokens)

4) Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Pricing varies: one-time deployment fee + annual platform license. Typical entry: $150k-$250k upfront + $20k-$40k/mo for managed control plane and support (wide range depending on on-prem hardware choices).
- Pros: strongest data isolation and control; required for some legal/regulatory setups.
- Cons: longer lead time, ops responsibility (unless we provide managed on-prem).

Rough recommendation: Given your volumes (1.44B tokens/month), Dedicated reserved capacity (12-24mo commit) is likely the most cost-effective while preserving predictable latency and data control. Hosted becomes expensive at that scale unless you prefer zero ops and flexible burst-only usage. Private/VPC is a go if legal/regulatory requires customer-managed infra.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_pricing_v1.xlsx (detailed line items), Hosted_vs_Dedicated_cost_model.pdf (scenario charts).

Next step: propose a 30-minute call to review the spreadsheet and pick a commit scenario. I'm available Tue/Wed next week 10-12 PT.
